title: Principles for constructing a Lewis diagram
body: The established principles used to construct the Lewis diagram of a molecule or polyatomic ion.

items.label: Count every valence electron
items.meaning: The diagram shows all valence electrons of the species: the sum for its atoms, plus one for each unit of negative charge or minus one for each unit of positive charge.

items.label: Join atoms with shared pairs
items.meaning: Bonded atoms share electron pairs (single, double or triple bonds); the remaining valence electrons appear as lone pairs.

items.label: Use the octet rule where possible
items.meaning: Each atom is given an octet of electrons where the electron count allows it (hydrogen has two); the octet rule is also a criterion for choosing among valid Lewis diagrams (2.6.A.2).

items.label: Show the charge of an ion
items.meaning: The diagram of a polyatomic ion is enclosed in brackets with the overall charge written outside the brackets.

caution: Topic 2.5 (2.5.A.1) says only that Lewis diagrams are constructed according to an established set of principles; the CED does not print them. The model has limits: a species with an odd number of valence electrons cannot satisfy the octet rule (2.6.A.3).
ced_evidence: 2.5.A.1: "Lewis diagrams can be constructed according to an established set of principles."
